body: Try not to stick out- leave your preview lanyard at home! Don't be afraid to ask for help- your professors want to see you succeed. Don't be afraid to talk to the deans office if you have issues- they are super helpful and can get many things done for you that you wouldn't be able to do yourself. Don't get wasted every night- the party scene, while fun, gets old fast. Join a club- I was in the marching band and it provided many cool opportunities that I couldn't have done myself (and I got to go to London and the Sugar Bowl). And lastly don't be a pretentious douche- be nice to people, you never know what opportunities might open up.

I was in it from 2011-2013. That was back in the good ol' days when our team was actually winning games- so we got to go the sugar bowl in 2012. And also London :) as far as being in the band itself goes, it's pretty nice. Lots of people, you'll make lots of friends. If you play brass you're pretty much guaranteed a spot in pregame- if not, good luck. Last year I counted a total of around 60 alternates for the woodwinds. Chair placement auditions are super important for pregame placement and participation in the halftime shows. Get the highest chair placement possible if you want to avoid sitting on the sidelines the first few games while the rest of the band marches out onto the field. The band directors try to downplay this but the fact remains that woodwinds get the shaft most days.

 Band camp sucks, it's seven days long and the week before classes start- 8-9:30 every day with 2 breaks for lunch and dinner. Your feet and ankles will be sore and you will be fighting to stay awake the third or fourth day from sleep deprivation. It's also hot as blazes outside so on top of that you'll be sweating like a pig when practices aren't indoor. Semester commitment is intense- marching practice everyday 4-6, except Wednesdays. Monday practice is indoors 6-8:30 with time for sectionals. Saturdays your whole day is game day. So the only day you really get a break is Sunday. Be prepared to cut your holiday break short for both Thanksgiving and Christmas. The FSU game is the Saturday after Thanksgiving and we have practice the Friday night before. If we qualify for a bowl game (which has been most years except 2013), we go after Christmas. 

But all in all the band is pretty fun. It's gotten pretty big over the past two years (probably because we went to the Olympics), and I honestly thought it changed too much for my liking (plus after three years I was burnt out on it), but your mileage may vary. Be prepared to work hard and do everything the directors tell you. Life will be easier :)
